question: A recruiting team answers similar candidate questions every week and re-pastes the same rubric and tone rules into every new chat. Which two moves fit the available features? Select two.
options: A) Ask Claude at the end of each chat to remember the rubric for whichever chat opens next.
B) Move the rubric and the tone rules into a Project, so each chat starts from that context.
C) Run every one of the candidate questions through Research mode so answers arrive with citations.
D) Keep the reusable reply template as an artifact the team can open and edit between chats.
E) Keep one very long running chat open so the rubric stays somewhere in the history above.
correct_answers: B) Move the rubric and the tone rules into a Project, so each chat starts from that context.
D) Keep the reusable reply template as an artifact the team can open and edit between chats.
explanations: Incorrect. A request made inside one chat does not durably carry team context into the next one; that is what a Project is for.
Correct. A Project is the feature for recurring work that needs shared context, so the rubric and tone rules stop being re-pasted every week.
Incorrect. Research mode is for agentic multi-step investigation of open questions, not for applying a known internal rubric.
Correct. The reply template is self-contained content the team returns to and edits, which is what an artifact is for.
Incorrect. One ever-growing chat pushes against the context limit and still leaves the rubric buried instead of durably configured.
